description:
Redwood Inference’s Optimize product can apply cost-saving configuration changes (batching, caching, quantization profiles) that materially affect model outputs. This project, “Quality guardrails gating for optimize,” adds mandatory quality evaluation checks and regression thresholds before any Optimize recommendation can be applied (automatically or via one-click) to production traffic.

Goals:
- Prevent silent quality regressions caused by cost optimizations (e.g., more aggressive batching, cache changes, or quantization profile switches).
- Define consistent, measurable quality gates (offline evals + online canary signals) with clear pass/fail criteria.
- Provide a traceable approval/audit trail: what changed, why it was suggested, which evals ran, and who approved/overrode.
- Keep developer experience fast: make “safe-by-default” the path while allowing documented exceptions.

Scope (in-scope):
- Config change types: batching policy updates, prefix/KV caching settings, and quantization profile changes (per model family/hardware SKU).
- Gating pipeline: trigger eval runs on proposed config diffs; compute quality deltas vs baseline; enforce thresholds; surface results in Console/Optimize.
- Rollout integration: require gates before enabling a canary rollout; block full rollout on failures; auto-rollback hooks.
- Observability: dashboards/alerts for gate failures, flaky evals, and drift; logging of gate decisions.

Out of scope (initially):
- Full private/on-prem automation (will be designed but delivered later); manual workflow + documentation first.
- New model onboarding process overhaul (only integrate with existing eval harness and prompt sets).

Key stakeholders and roles:
- Product: Aditya Rao (Optimize) owns PRD and launch; Paula Mendes (Rollouts/telemetry) owns rollout coupling.
- Applied ML / Evals: Jonas Weber, Karthik Iyer, Selene Huang own gate metrics, eval methodology, and prompt-set coverage.
- Runtime: Mateo Alvarez / Noah Patel / Sofia Ivanova ensure config diffs map cleanly to runtime behavior and have safe fallbacks.
- SRE/Observability: Sean Gallagher / Allison Grant define SLO impact signals, dashboards, and alerting; Connor O’Brien + Sahana Iyer support CI integration.

Phases & timeline (plausible):
- Discovery + requirements (2025-10 to 2025-11): define gate metrics, thresholds, supported config types, and exception policy.
- Design (2025-11 to 2025-12): architecture, data model (gate runs, baselines), integration points (Optimize service, eval-harness, Console), and rollout coupling.
- Implementation + internal beta (2026-01): gating enforced in staging + select internal workloads; fix flakiness and runtime edge cases.
- Limited production rollout (2026-02): enforce gates for Optimize changes in hosted API for a subset of routes/accounts.
- GA + expansion (2026-03+): extend to Dedicated defaults and broader model families; private workflow support.

Constraints / non-functional requirements:
- Eval runtime and cost must be bounded (tiered gates: fast smoke gates vs full gates).
- Statistical rigor: handle variance; require minimum sample sizes; track and mitigate flaky prompt sets.
- Backwards compatibility: existing manual config changes must be supported but logged and (where possible) gated.
- Clear override mechanics: time-bound exceptions with explicit owners and follow-ups.

files.description: PRD for quality gating in Optimize: user stories (one-click apply, auto-apply), supported config types, MVP vs v1, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and metrics (cost saved vs quality protected).

End-to-end design spec: services involved (Optimize, eval-harness, Console, rollout controller), data model for gate runs, APIs, state machine (pending/running/passed/failed/overridden), and failure modes.
Definition of quality metrics (task success, rubric scores, model-specific heuristics), regression thresholds, confidence/variance handling, and required coverage per prompt set.
Plan to curate/extend prompt sets for gating: workload categories, sampling strategy, golden outputs, known hard cases, and ownership for ongoing maintenance.
Interface contract between Optimize and eval-harness: inputs (config diff, baseline), required outputs (score deltas, artifacts), SLAs, retry rules, and versioning.
ADR documenting the decision to require eval gates before applying cost optimizations, including alternatives considered (monitor-only, post-deploy rollback), and rationale.
Standard metrics/logs/traces for gate runs: pass/fail rates, flake rate, latency/cost of evals, and how to attribute changes to routes/models/accounts.
Operational runbook for gate failures: triage steps, distinguishing real regressions vs eval flakiness, rollback/disable procedures, and escalation paths.
Playbook for investigating regressions triggered by batching/caching/quant profile changes; includes minimal reproduction setup and which artifacts to collect.
Policy for overrides: who can approve, time bounds, required evidence, audit requirements, and post-override follow-up tasks.
Dashboard requirements and mock layout: gate run funnel, failures by config type/model family, flakiness signals, and linked drill-down to artifacts.
Beta release notes for internal/limited customers: what changed, behavior when a gate fails, known limitations, and how to request an exception.
PM working doc: MVP scope decisions, open questions (fast vs full gates), edge cases, and draft customer messaging.
Applied ML scratchpad: threshold calibration experiments, variance analysis, notes on metric sensitivity for quantization vs caching changes.
Draft metric names/tags, example queries, and alert candidates; includes notes about avoiding alert storms from flaky eval suites.
Early UX notes for how gate results appear in Console: pass/fail summary, artifacts links, comparisons, and override workflow prompts.
Release/CI plan: how gate-related tests run in CI, required checks, how to handle GPU scarcity for eval jobs, and fallback strategies.
Oncall prep checklist for the rollout of gating: new alerts, runbooks, dashboards, and rehearsal scenarios.
Runtime team notes: mapping Optimize config diffs to runtime knobs; catalog of unsafe combinations; suggestions for validation before eval runs.
PM ticket tracking PRD completion, launch sequencing (internal beta → limited GA), and cross-functional sign-offs.
Engineering ticket for adding gate-run state machine, persistence, and API endpoints; includes subtasks and dependencies.
Ticket to implement/extend eval-harness endpoints to accept config diffs + baseline and return structured results/artifacts.
Ticket for a fast gate tier (small prompt subset) for quick feedback; defines target runtime, retry rules, and minimum coverage.
Ticket covering quantization-specific baseline logic (per GPU SKU/model family), required eval suites, and compatibility checks.
Console ticket: add UI elements to show gate status, block apply when failing, and provide links to artifacts and override request flow.
Ticket for emitting metrics/traces, building dashboards, and wiring alerting for failure spikes and flakiness.
Ticket to add audit log events (gate started/completed, pass/fail, override granted) for enterprise traceability.
Ticket integrating gate results with rollout promotion logic; defines behavior for canary halt, rollback triggers, and notifications.
Ticket to detect flaky suites, quarantine prompt sets, and provide tooling for reruns with attribution and variance tracking.
Ticket adding static validation (unsupported combos, safety constraints) before running expensive evals.
Design ticket: UX flows and copy for gate results, warnings, and override confirmation; includes review comments from PM/Eng.
PM ticket defining exception rules, approvers, and how exceptions are represented in UI/audit logs.
Ticket to enforce required CI checks for codepaths touching gating, including integration tests and schema validation.
PR implementing gate-run state machine and persistence in the Optimize service, with initial API endpoints and migration notes.
PR adding a typed config-diff schema, static validation rules, and rejection reasons used before eval execution.
PR to eval-harness adding an endpoint to run evals given a config diff + baseline; returns structured metrics and artifact pointers.
PR adding flakiness scoring, automatic rerun policy, and result aggregation logic for gate runs.
PR wiring Optimize to call eval-harness, manage retries, timeouts, and capture artifacts; includes failure-mode handling.
PR enforcing gating at the ‘apply config’ boundary; returns explicit failure reasons and links to gate run results.
PR implementing overrides (time-bound), approval recording, and emitting audit events; includes admin-only guardrails.
PR integrating gate results into canary promotion logic; prevents promotion on failure and posts notifications.
PR adding dashboards and alert rules for gate runs (pass rate, failure spikes, latency, flake rate) and runbook links.

PR extending Console/Optimize APIs to return gate result summaries and artifact URLs (or ids) for UI consumption.
Docs PR: internal/external-facing documentation draft explaining gating, how to interpret results, and how to request overrides.
PR adding end-to-end tests covering config diff → eval run → pass/fail → apply blocked/allowed, including override path.
PR adding a canary pipeline stage that verifies gate enforcement behavior and reports regressions in gating reliability.
PR enabling per-route/account-tier gating policy (e.g., self-serve vs enterprise) and default policies.
PR instrumenting gate execution paths with metrics, tracing spans, and structured logs for debugging.
Bugfix PR addressing a cancelation/race condition found during beta; includes post-incident notes and regression test.
PR adding admin tooling and flags to quarantine flaky suites and record reason codes.
